status: EXPERIMENTAL. Biodata items are scored empirically: weights are learned from outcomes, not set in advance. Until the outcome engine has data, use them only as evidence shown to the user ('You have competed at national level') and as features for the model.
evidence: Empirically keyed biodata is among the stronger predictors of job performance in the Sackett et al. (2022) revision.
design_rules: Ask about past, verifiable-in-principle behaviour, not opinions. Avoid items that proxy protected characteristics (family income, nationality, health).
free_text_coding: Code free-text answers with an LLM into the lane taxonomy and store both the raw text and the codes. Show the user the coding and let them correct it.

items.text: Before you turned 16, how many times did you earn money on your own initiative (selling things, doing jobs, online projects)?
Have you ever sold something to a stranger face to face or over the phone?
options: It has been part of my job

items.text: What is the highest level you have competed at in any organized sport, game or contest?
What is the largest audience that has seen something you made and published (video, writing, music, art, code)?
How many times have you led a group where others depended on your decisions (captain, club, project, shift)?
How often have teachers, coaches or managers picked you for extra responsibility?
Is there an activity you have spent more than about 1,000 hours on outside school or work? Which?
How many projects have you started that nobody asked you to do, and then finished?
What is the longest you have kept up a self-directed practice routine (training, an instrument, a skill)?
Have you taught or coached someone else in a skill, formally or informally?
Have you built or repaired something physical from scratch (furniture, an engine, a structure)?
options: It's a regular hobby or job

items.text: Have you made money from trading, investing, or games of skill? (Answer honestly; there is no right answer.)
In which school subjects were you among the best in your class? (Select all that apply.)
Between ages 12 and 16, what did you spend most of your free time on? (Select up to 3.)
options: Reading and learning on my own

items.text: In which activities do you most often lose track of time? Describe up to three.
In jobs, teams or school, what have people repeatedly asked you to do more of?
What have other people told you that you seem naturally good at?
Think of things you started and later quit. What was the most common reason?
options: Got bored once it became routine
Lost to others and lost interest
